briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 5, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Heatwaves and Worsening Climate Disasters
sections.content: Today, record-breaking heatwaves and the intensification of climate disasters across the globe and on the Korean Peninsula were reported as major news. Domestically, record heatwaves continued in Yesan County and throughout the Seoul Metropolitan Area, with Seoul experiencing its first-ever severe heatwave alert, where the sensible temperature approached 40°C. This led to 186 heat-related illnesses and an estimated 19 deaths [3, 28, 29]. In Daegu, 'climate vulnerable' individuals sought refuge in underground spaces to escape the heat, while Chungcheongbuk-do even deployed snowplows to cool down the extreme temperatures [27, 31]. Internationally, severe heatwaves in the UK and Europe saw a record high of 53°C recorded in a London playground, with an estimated 20,000 deaths across Europe alone. Wildfires and extreme weather were identified as the result of 'unequivocal climate change' [57, 64, 65]. This rapid acceleration of global warming, potentially pushing climate ecosystems beyond a critical threshold via a Super El Niño, is having widespread impacts, including a reshaping of global seaweed bloom maps, changes in Canadian river flows, and increased turbulence during flights [44, 46, 48, 54, 61].

sections.title: ⚠️ Delayed Climate Action and Pressures for Industrial Transition
sections.content: Despite severe climate disasters, concerns have been raised that policy implementation for climate change response remains insufficient. Criticism emerged that carbon neutrality policies are inadequately executed even as the Korean Peninsula boils, and ministries are making little progress despite strong directives from the State Council [13]. Meanwhile, Samjong KPMG analyzed that the net-zero competition is expanding beyond simple carbon neutrality to a struggle for industrial hegemony, emphasizing the need to integrate carbon, energy, and data in this era's 'green war' [8, 10]. The domestic Climate Minister announced that public discourse would begin on whether to include nuclear power plants and SMRs in the 12th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand, signaling ongoing discussions on the direction of energy transition [32]. Internationally, opinions were presented that companies might retreat from climate change response, and the European Central Bank (ECB) warned that climate change threatens the global economy even amidst a surging stock market [33, 51].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Amidst the climate crisis, positive movements towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition are being observed. President Lee emphasized that a renewable energy-centric transition is inevitable and that solar farming must be utilized to prevent regional decline. Assemblyman Park Hee-seung proposed a special law for renewable energy self-sufficient cities to establish a 'local production for local consumption' energy system [16, 18, 19]. The Ministry of Climate is pushing for the early achievement of 100GW of renewable energy, and Siheung City is promoting 'Siheung-type RE100,' encompassing everything from solar panel installation to RE100 [20, 21, 23]. Incheon Pentaport achieved a carbon-neutral practice by reducing 2.7 tons of disposable waste, and local community efforts continue, with Hoengseong County launching a reusable cup circulation service [5, 15]. Furthermore, Professor Ahn Jin-ho's team at Seoul National University identified the 'fingerprint' of automotive greenhouse gases, enhancing the accuracy of emission source tracking, while KOSPO and Jeju National University agreed to expand industry-academia cooperation for carbon neutrality [4, 11].

sections.title: 🌱 Exploring Climate Adaptation and Nature-Based Solutions
sections.content: The importance of climate adaptation and nature-based solutions is also being highlighted. European bison are gaining attention for their potential as 'natural firefighters' in the era of climate crisis, demonstrating how natural ecosystems can contribute to climate change mitigation [1]. Domestically, Incheon City is operating a carbon-neutral living lab with young people to improve the Songdo bicycle path, and the Incheon Carbon Neutral Youth Supporters are promoting a living lab for bicycle road revitalization, continuing citizen-participatory adaptation efforts [6, 14]. On Energy Day, the Gangwon National University Chuncheon Carbon Neutrality Support Center operated a citizen-participatory 'Energy React Project' to encourage local community engagement in climate action [12]. Internationally, Ghana's Environmental Protection Agency finalized comprehensive methane guidelines for the oil and gas sector, laying the groundwork for climate action in West Africa, and various adaptation efforts are underway, including a climate change program exploring solutions at its autumn workshop [37, 47].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Response to Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change is having significant impacts across various sectors of the international community, and response efforts are ongoing. Research has been published indicating that climate change is altering malaria activity in Africa, and Spain's Port of Avilés plans to rebuild its breakwater in preparation for storms brought by climate change [35, 56]. Furthermore, climate change is reshaping Canada's housing market, and in Canada, the vertical farming revolution is gaining attention as a way to bolster national food security amidst climate change [55, 59]. An unusual case was also reported where an island nation is offering 'golden passports' for $90,000 to fund its fight against climate change [52]. Legal and political discussions are also active, with attorneys general requesting Supreme Court justices to allow state courts to decide Boulder's climate change lawsuit [38]. ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) provides an important framework for these overarching climate and sustainability discussions [2].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the record-breaking heatwaves sweeping across the globe, the resulting disaster situations, and the efforts and policy challenges various nations face in responding to them. Addressing the climate crisis is no longer a choice but a matter of survival, and more robust and integrated action is urgently needed. This concludes the climate briefing for August 5, 2026.
